notes: Only the LIVE eval discriminated. Both fixture evals scored identically (11/11 and 8/8) in both configurations - the traps are visible when all the evidence sits in three tidy files, so they test reasoning rather than research discipline.

The live eval discriminated decisively and on the assertion that mattered: the baseline never reached Jet2holidays and recommended easyJet at GBP 2,247. Jet2 was GBP 2,028. The skill's 'one recon pass across ALL providers before depth' is the instruction that produced the difference.

The baseline correctly predicted its own failure: 'Jet2holidays not reached at all... it's the one real remaining chance of beating easyJet. Worth 10 minutes.' It identified the risk and ran out of budget before closing it.
Jet2 = GBP 2,028 was independently corroborated by two separate peer Claude sessions, so the with-skill answer is externally verified rather than self-reported.
Cost of the win: +9% tokens and roughly double the wall-clock on the live task (36 min vs 19 min). On a low-stakes purchase that ratio would not be worth it - the skill should probably say so.
